properties_verified.test_file: covered transitively via tests/test_hybrid_layer.py + tests/test_csa_compression.py + tests/test_mhc_sinkhorn.py
checks: no dedicated test file: this mechanism is a narrative/genealogy claim (MLA compresses KV *dimension*, DSA/CSA-indexer selects blocks, CSA/HCA compress *sequence length*) rather than a distinct piece of code -- its only testable surface is the same get_dsv4_compress_ratio / build_layer_spec switch table exercised by test_hybrid_layer.py's test_get_dsv4_compress_ratio_* and test_build_layer_spec_* (CSA layers get an Indexer, mirroring DSA's top-k reuse; HCA layers do not, mirroring 'compression is enough once m' is large'), and the CSA/HCA compression identity itself in test_csa_compression.py. Per dossier this mechanism has difficulty='supporting' and needs_worked_example=false, matching ch32's precedent for structural mechanisms with no independent numerical claim.

test_dense_baseline_layer_cost_stores_full_sequence: dense_baseline_layer_cost's kv_entries_stored == seq_len and flops_per_token == seq_len*head_dim exactly, i.e. the vanilla O(L) storage / O(L) per-token FLOPs tax the motivation section names is reproduced as a closed form, not just asserted in prose
test_csa_layer_cost_kv_scales_with_1_over_m: compress_ratio m=4 halves-then-halves-again (quarters) the KV entries stored versus m=1, confirming the O(L) -> O(L/m) storage reduction claim
test_hca_layer_cost_kv_scales_with_1_over_m_prime: kv_entries_stored == seq_len/128 exactly for HCA, confirming O(L) -> O(L/m') at the larger compression rate

test_csa_layer_cost_flops_independent_of_seq_len_for_core_attn_but_indexer_scales: isolates that core-attention FLOPs is O(k) (independent of L) while the indexer's scan of all L/m candidate blocks is the one seq_len-dependent term -- this is exactly the 'two separate ledgers, don't conflate' warning the file's own PAPER comment (echoing ch32's cost-model lesson) makes explicit

test_overlap_transform_shape_and_borrow_pattern: hand-traced n=6,m=2 example verifies the exact 'own a-values [m:2m) + borrowed b-values from the *previous* block [0:m)' index pattern of Eq.11's bracketed 2m window, including the i=0 zero-padding case
test_softmax_over_positions_handles_neg_inf_padding: -inf padded positions get exactly-zero softmax weight with no NaN, matching the paper's explicit i=0 padding rule
test_weighted_pool_matches_manual_computation: Eq.12's Hadamard-product-then-sum (S ⊙ C, summed over the window) reproduced by hand for a 2-position window

test_csa_compress_sequence_soft_argmax_limit / test_hca_compress_sequence_soft_argmax_limit: engineering one position's bias to +50 (rest at -50) drives the compressed output to numerically coincide (atol=1e-3) with that single position's projected C value -- the most direct way to confirm Eq.11's Softmax_row is a genuine per-channel weighted selection over positions, not a plain scalar-attention average that the reader could otherwise misread it as

test_compressor_shape_csa / test_compressor_shape_hca: coff=1+overlap gives coff=2 for compress_ratio=4 (CSA, overlapped) and coff=1 for compress_ratio=128 (HCA, non-overlapped), matching the landing code's wkv/wgate output-dimension packing
test_overlap_transform_rejects_non_divisible_length / test_hca_compress_sequence_rejects_non_divisible_length / test_compressor_shape_rejects_unsupported_ratio: boundary/error-path coverage

test_index_score_relu_zeroes_negative_dot_products: a head with a negative q.k dot product contributes exactly 0 to the index score regardless of its weight (w=1000) -- confirms Eq.16 uses ReLU, not softmax or raw dot product, matching the paper's explicit 'ReLU for throughput' design choice
test_index_scores_for_query_matches_loop: batched scoring over all candidate compressed blocks matches a per-block loop (seed=0)

test_indexer_compressed_keys_shape: indexer key compression reuses the same csa_compress_sequence primitive (Eq.9-12) with the indexer's own weight set, output shape (n/m, c_idx) as the paper's 'same compression operation... to get compressed indexer keys' text specifies
test_topk_sparse_selection_picks_highest_scores: exact top-k index recovery on an engineered score vector, output ordered ascending as Eq.17 implies for downstream gather

test_topk_sparse_selection_respects_causal_limit: the globally-highest-scoring candidate (index 5) is correctly excluded when it falls outside the causal window s < floor(t/m) -- the causal constraint the paper states in prose is enforced, not just described
test_topk_sparse_selection_empty_causal_window / test_topk_sparse_selection_k_larger_than_candidates: boundary cases (t=0 causal window, k exceeding candidate count)

test_hca_compress_sequence_output_shape: non-overlapped compression to n/m' blocks (m'=4 substituted for the paper's 128 to keep tests fast; the compression formula itself is compression-rate-agnostic)
test_hca_compress_sequence_soft_argmax_limit: same soft-argmax-limit technique as CSA confirms Eq.22's Softmax_row is a genuine per-channel weighted selection for the non-overlapped HCA case too
test_compressor_shape_hca: overlap=False, coff=1 for compress_ratio=128 (no 2m window, matching Eq.20-23's single-pass compression)

HCA's dense core attention (Eq.26, 'does not employ sparse attention' -- attend to *all* compressed blocks) is exercised structurally via mqa_core_attention/attention_output_pipeline in tests/test_shared_mqa_grouped_output.py (same primitive CSA uses on its sparse subset; HCA callers pass the full kv_entries set instead of a top-k subset -- this is exactly how the dossier and impl-notes describe the CSA/HCA code-sharing)

test_get_dsv4_compress_ratio_reads_array / _none_config_is_dense / _out_of_range_is_dense: the per-layer switch table read (4=CSA, 128=HCA, unset/out-of-range=dense) matches vllm_ascend/utils.py:L105-110's get_dsv4_compress_ratio behavior exactly, including the MTP-layer-as-dense fallback

test_build_layer_spec_csa_has_compressor_and_indexer / _hca_has_compressor_but_not_indexer / _dense_has_neither: the compressor/indexer mounting rule (CSA: both; HCA: compressor only; dense: neither) matches DeepseekV4Attention.__init__'s conditional module construction

test_build_model_layers_interleave: an 8-layer [4,4,4,128]*2 config produces exactly the interleaved [CSA,CSA,CSA,HCA,CSA,CSA,CSA,HCA] kind sequence -- directly demonstrates the layer-level interleaving the mechanism is about

test_kv_cache_spec_for_layer_dense_uses_swa / _csa_hca_use_mla_with_ratio: dense layers route to an independent SWA cache while CSA/HCA layers route to an MLA-style cache tagged with their compress_ratio, matching DSAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec's branch
test_build_layer_spec_rejects_unsupported_ratio: boundary/error path for an unsupported compress_ratio

test_hybrid_stack_average_cost_mixes_csa_hca: a 2-layer [4,128] stack's averaged cost exactly equals the arithmetic mean of the standalone CSA and HCA layer costs -- confirms the per-layer-then-average accounting method is correct before it's used for any ratio claim
test_hybrid_stack_average_cost_treats_le_1_as_dense / _rejects_unsupported_ratio: config validation boundaries
test_relative_efficiency_ratio_less_than_one_when_hybrid_cheaper: a hybrid [4,4,4,128]-layer stack's flops_ratio and kv_ratio versus a dense baseline both land strictly between 0 and 1

test_mixed_precision_kv_bytes_less_than_pure_bf16: BF16-RoPE/FP8-rest mixed storage strictly beats pure-BF16 storage for the same KV entry count, matching §2.3.4's 'reduces the KV cache size by nearly half' claim's direction (not magnitude)

test_worked_example_efficiency_produces_sub_one_ratios_and_is_honest_about_scope: with an illustrative (not DeepSeek's undisclosed) [4,4,4,128]-repeated config and seq_len=1e6, the hybrid stack's FLOPs and KV ratios are both strictly between 0 and 1 versus both the dense baseline and the CSA-degenerate (m=1) DSA-only baseline -- proves the qualitative claim 'hybrid beats both baselines' the paper's 27%/10% figures assert directionally, while impl-notes.md and the module docstring both explicitly disclaim reproducing the literal 27%/10% percentages (which require an undisclosed full deployment config) -- this is the deliberate, correctly-scoped honesty the anti-fabrication rule requires for a primer chapter's numeric worked example
test_attention_queries_reshape: low-rank query upcast reshapes into (n_heads, head_dim) correctly

test_mqa_core_attention_shared_kv_across_heads: with a single KV entry, every query head's output collapses exactly to that entry (softmax degenerates to weight 1) -- confirms all heads truly share one KV set (MQA), not per-head independent KV as in standard MHA

test_mqa_core_attention_empty_kv_returns_zeros / test_mqa_core_attention_softmax_normalizes: boundary case + a convex-hull norm-bound sanity check that the softmax output is a genuine convex combination of KV rows

test_grouped_output_projection_shape_and_value: hand-computed reference (split heads into g groups, each group's flattened output projected down to d_g, concatenated, then projected to d) matches the function's output exactly -- verifies Eq.18-19's grouped-output-projection machinery bit-for-bit
test_grouped_output_projection_rejects_indivisible_groups: error path when n_heads is not divisible by group count
test_attention_output_pipeline_end_to_end_shape: the full query->core-attention->grouped-output pipeline composes correctly end to end

properties_verified.property_kind: identity + degenerate-case (both extremes of the sink mass)
checks: test_sliding_window_recent_kv_basic / _clamped_at_sequence_start: the recent-n_win-token window is exactly right at an interior position and correctly clamped (no negative indices) near sequence start

test_attention_sink_scores_sum_less_than_one_when_sink_dominates: a dominant sink logit (10.0 vs uniform 1.0 logits) drives >90% of the softmax mass into the sink term, i.e. the attention scores over real candidates sum to <0.1 -- directly demonstrates Eq.27's headline claim that a query head 'can adjust its total attention scores to be... near 0'

test_attention_sink_scores_reduces_to_plain_softmax_when_sink_negligible: with sink_logit=-1000 the scores match plain softmax over the real logits to 1e-6 -- confirms the sink term correctly vanishes at the opposite extreme rather than always perturbing the distribution
test_sink_absorbed_mass_is_complement_of_score_sum: sink_absorbed_mass is exactly 1 - sum(scores) by construction, algebraic identity check
test_apply_partial_rope_leaves_head_untouched: the first d-rope_dims dimensions are exactly unchanged, only the last rope_dims are rotated, matching '...apply RoPE to its last 64 dimensions'

test_apply_partial_rope_preserves_norm_of_rotated_part: RoPE is an orthogonal rotation, so the full vector's norm is preserved -- a strong structural check that the rotation matrix construction (_rope_rotation_matrix) is a genuine orthogonal transform, not an approximation

test_apply_partial_rope_zero_position_is_identity: position=0 gives cos=1,sin=0 for every frequency, so the rotated tail equals the input tail exactly (atol=1e-10) -- a degenerate-case sanity check on the frequency/angle construction
test_apply_partial_rope_rejects_rope_dims_too_large: error path when rope_dims exceeds vector dimension

test_apply_output_relative_rope_uses_negative_position: apply_output_relative_rope(vec, query_position=7) exactly equals apply_partial_rope(vec, position=-7) -- confirms the output-side 'RoPE with position -i' step is implemented as literally negating the query's own position, which is impl-notes.md's explicitly-flagged reading of the paper's ambiguous overloaded index notation (i as both head index and position) -- test and docstring both make this documented interpretive choice traceable rather than silently baked in
test_kvcomp_config_defaults: chunk_size=128, chunk_repre_method='max', must_select_blocks=[0,-2,-1] match the landing dataclass defaults verbatim

test_chunk_representative_max_min_sum / _rejects_unknown_method: all three chunk-representative reduction methods produce correct per-dimension max/min/sum, plus the error path for an unsupported method name
test_kvcomp_metadata_defaults: sink=1, recent=4 match initialize_kvcomp_metadata's fixed runtime constants

test_qr_orthogonal_random_weights_are_orthonormal_columns: W^T @ W == I within 1e-8 -- confirms the QR-orthogonalized hash projection actually produces orthonormal columns as the landing code's _init_hash_weights intends
test_qr_orthogonal_random_weights_rejects_dim_in_smaller_than_hash_bits: boundary/error path for the reduced-QR precondition
test_hash_encoder_output_shape_and_dtype / _rejects_hash_bits_not_multiple_of_8: hash_bits must be byte-aligned (8-divisible) to pack into uint8, matching npu_sign_bits_pack's packing granularity
test_hash_encoder_identical_inputs_produce_identical_codes: determinism check

test_unpack_hash_recovers_sign_pattern: pack-then-unpack round trip through an identity projection recovers the exact +-1 sign pattern of the raw input -- confirms compute_hash/unpack_hash are true inverses of the sign-bit encoding, not merely 'shaped correctly'
test_hamming_distance_packed_zero_for_identical_codes / _counts_differing_bits: exact bit-count verification (3 differing bits in 0b00000111) of the XOR+popcount distance metric

test_must_select_indices_for_sink_and_recent / _handles_small_num_blocks: sink=1,recent=4 maps to indices [0,6,7,8,9] for a 10-block sequence, and correctly collapses to 'all blocks' when sink+recent >= num_blocks

test_select_topk_blocks_by_hamming_forces_must_select: with the true nearest block (distance 0) at index 3 and top_k=1, the selection still force-includes must_select_blocks=[0,-1] -- confirms sink/recent blocks are never dropped by the LSH approximation even when top_k alone would exclude them
test_select_topk_blocks_by_hamming_no_must_select: baseline top-1 selection picks the genuinely closest block by Hamming distance

test_mixed_precision_kv_bytes_less_than_pure_bf16: BF16-for-RoPE-dims/FP8-for-rest storage strictly beats pure-BF16 storage byte count at equal KV entry count and total dimension, matching §2.3.4's 'hybrid representation reduces the KV cache size by nearly half compared with pure BF16 storage' claim's direction

test_kv_cache_spec_for_layer_dense_uses_swa / _csa_hca_use_mla_with_ratio (test_hybrid_layer.py): the four-kv-cache-type routing (dense->SWA; CSA/HCA->MLA tagged with their own compress_ratio, i.e. two distinct compressed-state cache shapes) is exercised, matching DSV4_BLOCK_SIZES' four-entry block-size table and DSAAttention.get_kv_cache_spec's branch
test_hc_residual_update_matches_eq1: X_{l+1} = B_l@X_l + C_l@F_l_out reproduced by hand for a small 3-hyperconnection example (Eq.1 identity)
test_layer_input_is_weighted_average: A_l@X_l as the actual sub-layer input, hand-verified
test_is_doubly_stochastic_true_for_identity / _false_for_arbitrary_matrix: the Birkhoff-polytope membership predicate correctly accepts the identity matrix and rejects a non-doubly-stochastic matrix

test_rms_norm_flatten_unit_rms: flatten-then-RMSNorm produces RMS==1.0 exactly (eps=0), confirming it normalizes the whole n_hc*d vector jointly (not per-row) as the paper's hat-X_l = RMSNorm(vec(X_l)) specifies

test_sinkhorn_knopp_converges_to_doubly_stochastic: 20 iterations of alternating column/row normalization on a random 5x5 matrix converges to a doubly-stochastic matrix within atol=1e-4 (seed=0) -- the central numerical claim of Eq.8

test_sinkhorn_knopp_more_iterations_converge_more_tightly: 20 iterations produce strictly smaller row/column-sum deviation than 1 iteration (seed=1) -- monotonic convergence property, not just an endpoint check
test_apply_sigmoid_constraints_ranges: A_l in [0,1], C_l in [0,2] with midpoint values (0.5, 1.0) at logit=0, confirming Eq.6-7's sigmoid/2*sigmoid range constraints exactly
test_dynamic_raw_params_shapes: the three dynamic-parameter projections (A~,B~,C~) produce the correct shapes for a 3x4 hyperconnection state

test_apply_constraints_end_to_end_produces_valid_hc_params: full dynamic-params -> sigmoid+Sinkhorn pipeline (seed=4) produces a simultaneously valid A_l in [0,1], C_l in [0,2], and doubly-stochastic B_l -- end-to-end Eq.3-8 correctness

notes: All 14 dossier mechanisms have direct or transitive test coverage (genealogy-mla-dsa-csa-hca is a narrative/structural mechanism with no unique code of its own -- difficulty='supporting', needs_worked_example=false in dossier -- and is covered transitively through the same hybrid_layer/csa_compression/mhc_sinkhorn tests used for its sibling mechanisms, following ch32's precedent for structural mechanisms). 89/89 tests pass on host with a pure-NumPy implementation (no vllm/vllm_ascend/torch_npu import anywhere in implementation/, confirmed by grep). The chapter's central anti-fabrication commitment -- not reproducing the paper's literal '27% FLOPs / 10% KV' percentages, since DeepSeek never published the full deployment config (per-layer compress_ratios array, per-layer k, indexer head counts) needed to rederive them -- is enforced both in the implementation docstrings/impl-notes.md and verified by test_worked_example_efficiency_produces_sub_one_ratios_and_is_honest_about_scope, which only asserts the qualitative 'hybrid beats both baselines' direction, matching the property_kind classification the tester agent contract calls for on optimization-type mechanisms in primer chapters. One documented interpretive choice (apply_output_relative_rope's reading of the paper's overloaded index 'i' as query position rather than head index) is explicitly flagged in both the implementation comment and impl-notes.md rather than silently resolved, and its test (test_apply_output_relative_rope_uses_negative_position) verifies internal consistency of that reading, not the paper's intended notation (which the excerpt does not itself disambiguate).
